text: . Benchmark domestic equity indices ended 0.4% down today. The Sensex declined 307 points to close at 76,957. The Nifty dropped 95 points to settle at 24,800. Meanwhile, the broader market at the National Stock Exchange displayed a mixed trend. The Midcap 100 index gained 0.2%, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped 0.7 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened on a weak note as escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia and rising crude oil prices weighed on investor sentiment. Both the indices witnessed selling pressure across most sectors throughout the session.In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top underperformers, Adani Ports declined 4.1%, ITC dropped around 3.7%, and Bharti Airtel lost nearly 2.8%. In contrast, Sun Pharma gained 1.9%, ICICI Bank added 1.7%, and Axis Bank rose one and a half per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 21 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top laggards, Utilities decreased 2.6%, Metal lost 2.4%, and Services dipped 1.9%. In contrast, MidSmall Private Banks Quality Tilt rose over 1.2%, MidSmall Private Banks gained 1.2%, and Bankex added over 0.3%.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2572 companies declined, 1858 advanced and 250 remained unchanged.

. Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that as global companies reassess their supply chains and capital allocation, India offers not only the scale of a vast market but also the depth of a long-term investment and operating platform. She made these remarks while addressing a high-level Business Roundtable with leading investors and business leaders in Chicago, United States. She highlighted India’s broad-based growth, reform momentum and expanding opportunities for long-term investment.Ms Sitharaman also emphasised that India’s investment appeal lies in the convergence of scale, sustained economic growth, skilled talent, world-class infrastructure, technological advancement and a decade of consistent reforms.A key focus of the meeting was “Manufacture in India – for India and for the world”, with opportunities across manufacturing, AI and digital, financial services, infrastructure, food processing, defence and advanced technologies. Ms Sitharaman noted that India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC and India Stack, has created platforms operating at population scale. She added that the country’s next phase of growth lies in building high-value businesses in AI, engineering, analytics, product development, semiconductors and electronics, with Global Capability Centres increasingly evolving into global innovation hubs.Ms Sitharaman underlined that GIFT IFSC is emerging as an international financial centre connecting global capital with Indian opportunities. Referring to the reconfiguration of global supply chains, the Minister said India combines a large domestic market with globally competitive manufacturing capabilities, with the focus now shifting beyond assembly to deeper component manufacturing, engineering and advanced technologies, supported by Production Linked Incentive schemes.Highlighting initiatives such as Atmanirbhar Bharat and iDEX, Ms Sitharaman said India is strengthening domestic capabilities in drones, autonomous systems and other advanced technologies. She also invited global partners to co-develop, co-produce and build for global markets, urging them to view India not merely as a market to serve but as a platform from which to build for the world.The Roundtable was organised by the Consulate General of India in Chicago in association with the US-India Strategic Partnership Forum.

. In Squash, India’s Abhay Singh won the men’s singles title at the Tuanku Muhriz Trophy 2026 in Seremban, Malaysia, yesterday. The top-seeded Abhay defeated third-seeded Henry Leung of Hong Kong, China, 3-2 in the final of the PSA Challenger Tour 15 event.The victory marked the 27-year-old Indian squash player’s 13th PSA Tour title and his second of the year, following his win at the Indian Open in Mumbai in March. Abhay, at world No.24, is India’s highest-ranked men’s player. It was also Abhay Singh’s third Tuanku Muhriz Trophy title. He previously won the tournament in 2022 and 2024.Abhay, who won gold in the men’s team and bronze in mixed doubles at Hangzhou 2023, is also part of the Indian squash squad for the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya. He is slated to compete in the men’s singles and team events. Meanwhile, Rathika Suthanthira Seelan and Anika Dubey represented India in the women’s singles competition. Both bowed out in the round of 16. Squash is set to make its Olympic debut at LA 2028.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

. The United Arab Emirates has condemned an Iranian attack involving a drone that was intercepted by air defence systems over UAE territorial waters. In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) said that these hostile attacks constitute a dangerous escalation, an unacceptable act of aggression, and a direct threat to the UAE’s security, stability, and territorial integrity, in violation of the principles of international law and the Charter of the United Nations. The UAE underlined that it will not tolerate any threat to its security and sovereignty and that it reserves the right to respond to these attacks. The Ministry further stressed the need to immediately halt these attacks and ensure full compliance with the cessation of all hostilities.The UAE also condemned the Iranian attacks targeting Jordan with missiles. It reiterated the UAE’s full solidarity with Jordan and its support for all measures aimed at safeguarding its security and stability.In another statement, Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, Secretary General of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), also condemned the attacks and called on Iran to immediately halt such attacks and hostile acts. US & Iran exchanged military attacks today, in the first major escalation in almost a month. Oil prices, as seen through Brent crude futures and U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude, rose by 3%, following the latest reports on the escalation.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have remained net buyers of Indian equities so far in August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested 30, 919 crore rupees in the domestic stock market so far this month.Of the total investment, 18,791 crore rupees came through purchases on stock exchanges, while 12,128 crore rupees were invested through the primary market. The FPIs have extended their buying streak to a second consecutive month, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals, a stable rupee, strong quarterly earnings and a reversal in chip trade.Meanwhile, the debt market has witnessed a mixed trend in Foreign Portfolio Investors flows. So far in August, FPIs have infused 289 crore rupees in the debt securities through Voluntary Retention Route (VRR). The Fully Accessible Route (FAR) has seen inflows of 627 crore rupees during the period under review. In contrast, FPIs have withdrawn 2,318 crore rupees from the General Limit route.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit begins today in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. It is being held to mark the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. The theme of this year’s SCO summit is ‘25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity’. The SCO has 10 member countries, including India, China and Russia. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2017.Prime Minister Modi at the Summit venue received a warm welcome. PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping shook hands and interacted while walking together and were seen having a conversation after they posed for a group photograph with other leaders.

. Security personnel involved in rescue operations following devastating flash floods in Nepal are facing major challenges due to shortages of specialised equipment, body bags, ropes and helicopters. The floods, believed to have been triggered by a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, swept through the Bhotekoshi River corridor, destroying homes, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, NDRRMA, today said that the death toll has surged to 939, while more than 4,247 people remain untraceable. As many as 279 bodies were recovered in Chitawan district, 216 in Nawalparasi East, 168 in Nawalparasi West, 95 in Nuwakot, 65 in Gorkha, 55 in Dhading, 38 in Tanahu and 23 in Rasuwa.Personnel from the Nepal Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force have been deployed in large numbers across the affected areas. However, officials said the shortage of modern rescue equipment is making operations particularly difficult in dangerous terrain.Security personnel have also repeatedly sought helicopters to reach people trapped or stranded in remote areas. A police inspector said several people had contacted Police Control 100 for help, but rescuers were sometimes unable to reach them because of operational difficulties.Prime Minister Balendra Shah described the floods as an “unprecedented and devastating natural disaster”. Nearly 21,000 security personnel are involved in rescue operations. The Red Cross estimates that more than 90,000 people have been affected, while authorities continue efforts to recover and identify bodies.India has deployed specialised teams to assist Nepal with rescue operations and the identification of victims. A 19-member Indian forensics team began work in Kathmandu yesterday to support DNA analysis for identifying mortal remains. An Indian tunnel rescue team is also continuing operations at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang. Expert teams are helping Nepalese rescuers trace 933 workers and employees at various hydropower project sites who have been out of contact since August 26, with many believed to be trapped inside tunnels.

. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today informed that around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Singh said Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, NGEs to carry out various space activities. Out of these, 18 NGEs are start-ups. The Minister said the Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector. This is being done to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies. IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date, 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit at Bishkek in the Kyrgyz Republic today. The discussions focused on key areas of India-Russia bilateral cooperation, including trade and investment, energy and defence.During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi said it was a matter of deep satisfaction that cooperation between India and Russia continued to scale new heights.On the Ukraine conflict, Prime Minister Modi said, they must move from endless wars to ending wars, adding that India supports all efforts towards peace and will continue to do so.During the meeting, the Prime Minister said all Indians are eager to welcome President Putin to the BRICS Summit, which will be hosted in New Delhi in the coming days.President Vladimir Putin showed his satisfaction that Indian-Russian relations continue to strengthen on the basis of the principles of a special and privileged partnership.Prime Minister Modi also held bilateral meetings with leaders of Iran, Kyrgyz Republic and Armenia today. Mr Modi and Iran President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, during their meeting reviewed recent developments in the West Asia region and shared perspectives on the evolving situation. Mr Modi expressed concern at the escalation of tensions in the region and reiterated India’s consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. Calling for safeguarding the freedom of navigation and commerce, Mr Modi emphasized that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers must not be harmed under any circumstances.Prime Minister Modi and President of the Kyrgyz Republic Sadyr Zhaparov reviewed the progress in bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the Strategic Partnership between the two countries. Mr Modi and his Armenian counterpart, Nikol Pashinyan, during their talks, discussed ways to further strengthen bilateral cooperation across various areas including defence, economic, pharma, science and technology, culture and education.Earlier, on the first day of his visit to the Central Asian Country today, Prime Minister Modi interacted with the ‘Friends of India’ groups. Four delegations working with India in various fields were present on the occasion.Tomorrow, on the final day of his visit to Kyrgyz Republic, Prime Minister Modi will address the 26th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. Mr Modi reached Bishkek yesterday after concluding his successful visit to Uzbekistan.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. The Tata Institute of Social Sciences, TISS, conferred degrees on 1,376 students and scholars at its 86th annual convocation held in Mumbai yesterday.The degrees included those awarded to 35 doctoral scholars and graduates from Master’s, Bachelor’s, Integrated and dual-degree programmes.The first undergraduate batch of Analytics and Sustainability Studies also received their degrees. Director of Tata Memorial Hospital, Dr C. S. Pramesh, was the chief guest at the convocation.

. Indian table tennis player Ankur Bhattacharjee has won his maiden WTT men’s singles title at the WTT Feeder Olomouc tournament in Czechia. He also secured the men’s doubles gold with fellow Indian Akash Pal. World number 78 defeated third seed Slovenia’s Deni Kozul 3-1 in the singles final to complete a memorable campaign. Earlier, Ankur and Akash Pal defeated Hungary’s Csaba Andras Szantosi and Poland’s Alan Kulczycki Zalewski 3-1 in the men’s doubles final.Ankur, who was a finalist at the Europe Youth Smash in Sweden in 2025, had already reached two quarterfinals and two semifinals in 2026 before claiming his maiden WTT title in Olomouc.

. India’s Real GDP has observed a growth rate of 7.8% during the first quarter of the financial year 2026-27 compared to 6.9% during the same period of the previous financial year. The Indian Economy has sustained Growth Momentum despite Global Headwinds. The nominal GDP has also registered 10.3% growth during the first quarter of the current financial year. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today released the quarterly estimates of GDP for the first quarter from April to June of the current financial year. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation Secretary Dr Saurabh Garg said that growth across all sectors has been highly positive, which demonstrates that government interventions are having an impact, maintaining a positive growth rate despite shifts in the overall landscape and the geopolitical situation. He added that the service sector has performed exceptionally well, alongside the financial, housing, and real estate sectors.The Ministry informed that the Real Gross Value Added (GVA) in the first quarter of the current financial year has been assessed to grow by 8.2%, while the Nominal GVA has been assessed to grow by 11.5%. Furthermore, the tertiary sector has boosted the performance of the economy by registering growth of 10% at Constant prices, mainly driven by the Financial, Real Estate, IT and professional services sectors, which have observed 12.1% growth. Meanwhile, the secondary sector has registered a growth of 8.6% at Constant prices. The Ministry said that the primary sector has observed a 2.9% growth rate at constant prices, mainly contributed by the performance of the ‘Agriculture and Allied’ sector, which registered 3.6% growth during the first quarter of the current financial year.

. Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the Government of India is making every possible effort to provide assistance in the affected areas of Nepal, and the railways are also part of this effort. While virtually inaugurating the Nepalganj Road-Nanpara-Bahraich rail section today, the Union Minister said that Railway officials are continuously working in coordination with district and state authorities and the Ministry of External Affairs. He added that wherever rescued passengers have arrived, the Railways have made continuous efforts to help them reach their destinations.Union Railway Minister informed that the opening of the new rail section would provide passengers with more convenient transportation and boost regional connectivity and development. He added that with the completion of gauge conversion, several important locations, including Nanpara, Matera, Risiya, Bahraich, Babhanan, Nepalganj and Babaganj, would become better integrated with the wider railway network. Shri Vaishnaw also flagged off the Nepalganj Road-Varanasi City Special train on the newly inaugurated section. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also attended the inauguration programme held in Bahraich and said that the connectivity provided by the new rail section and train services is important not only for the security and convenience of the border areas but also for the overall prosperity of the region.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India’s economic growth of 7.8 per cent is a reflection of hard work and collective resolve of 140 crore citizens. Sharing a video in a social media post today, Mr Modi said that India is progressing at a fast pace despite global problems like ongoing wars and instability since the Covid-19 pandemic. He said in order to maintain this growth, it is important to become Atmanirbhar Bharat.The Prime Minister urged the citizens to adopt Swadeshi, promote Vocal for Local and support Made in India products. Mr Modi also urged the citizens to restrict foreign travel, avoid planning weddings in foreign countries and not buy gold if not necessary. Mr Modi expressed confidence that if all the citizens adopt the practice of Swadeshi, the vision of Viksit Bharat will be achieved in 100 years of independence.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has hailed India‘s exemplary GDP growth of 7.8% in the first quarter of Financial Year 2026-27. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that this achievement stands as a testament to the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, which has filled the nation with resilience to emerge successful despite severe global uncertainties. He congratulated every citizen on this remarkable achievement.

. India has strongly rejected a ruling by the World Bank-constituted Court of Arbitration over the Indus Waters Treaty, rejecting the tribunal’s authority and calling its decisions legally invalid. In a social media post, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said India has never recognised the arbitration panel, did not participate in its proceedings and would not be bound by its rulings. New Delhi also reiterated that the Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance.The statement came after the Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled that India’s reasons for putting the treaty on hold did not justify its suspension or termination. The panel called on India to continue observing its obligations under the 1960 water-sharing agreement. India, however, rejected the ruling, arguing that the arbitration panel itself was established in violation of the terms of the treaty. The MEA said the panel has no jurisdiction whatsoever over India’s sovereign decisions concerning the treaty or its infrastructure projects.New Delhi suspended the Indus Waters Treaty following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year, citing national security concerns and continued cross-border terrorism. India has maintained that its decision on the treaty is a sovereign matter and that statements or rulings by the arbitration panel will not affect its actions related to water and infrastructure projects.

. Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare J.P. Nadda today reviewed the progress of TB elimination efforts under PM-PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform for Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, with Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth. The meeting focused on strengthening inter-ministerial convergence for the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. Ministry of Health in a social media post said that the review emphasised measurable outcomes and tangible grassroots impact through early detection, prevention, community awareness, screening and sustained community mobilisaion. It added that the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through MY Bharat volunteers, and the Ministry of Defence through NCC cadets, are strengthening field-level outreach and awareness. Besides, educational institutions and workplaces are also being brought into the national effort, with ESIC strengthening TB screening and support for workers. The Ministry said that this whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach will further accelerate India’s collective efforts towards a TB Mukt Bharat, in line with the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

. In Duleep trophy cricket tournament, East Zone bundle out defending champion Central Zone for 266 on day one of the  semi-final match at Chennai today.Electing to bowl, East Zone’s pace attack exploited the favourable conditions from the outset to keep Central Zone under pressure throughout the day. Tripura medium-pacer Abhijit Sarkar was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 3 for 38.   For central zone  Rinku Singh scored  60 off 88 balls and Aryan Juyal’s 46 off 113 balls. East Zone set to begin their first innings on day two, where the pitch is expected to assist seam bowlers further.In another semifainal clash, opting to bat first, South Zone bowl out North Zone for a modest 195 on  day one  at Chennai today. Opening batter Qamran Iqbal provided the sole resistance for North Zone by compiling a gritty 76 off 182 balls. In reply, South Zone reached 40 for 2 at stumps, trailing North Zone by 155 runs. For south Zone, pacer Vidhwath Kaverappa picked a disciplined four-wicket haul to bowl out North Zone at a modest score.

. Sikkim Shooters performed extraordinarily in 13th North East Zone Shooting Championship 2026. 13th North East Zone Shooting Championship 2026 concluded yesterday at Guwahati, Assam.Laxuman Adhikari from Sikkim won a historic Bronze Medal in the Master Men’s 10m Air Pistol Individual category in this Championship. This was the first-ever medal won by a shooter representing Sikkim at the North East Zonal level.Two shooters from Sikkim Anu Chettri and Tshering Yangden Bhutia have qualified for the 69th National Shooting Championship 2026 after putting up strong performances in 13th North East Zonal Shooting Championship. Chettri secured qualification in the 10m air pistol event, while Bhutia has been selected in 10m air rifle.In total, 11 shooters from Sikkim competed at the Zonal Championship, with the Sikkim Rifle Association contingent comprising eight pistol shooters and three rifle shooters

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today interacted with the ‘Friends of India’ in Bishkek on the first day of his two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan. Four delegations working with India in various fields, including Yoga and Manas Academy, were present on the occasion.After this,  Prime Minister Modi paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at his statue situated at the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Park in Bishkek.The Prime Minister will also hold bilateral meetings today with leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states. These include meetings with the Heads of State of Russia, Iran, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia.Tomorrow, on the second and final day of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi will address the 26th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

. Ahead of Independence Day, a platform for creative expression has been provided to the youth in Uttar Pradesh. For this, the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign was launched. Under this campaign, the graffiti wall programme organised near Lucknow University today. Artists from the city painted public murals on the theme of a mafia-free and changing Uttar Pradesh. Through these paintings, the Uttar Pradesh of before 2017 and the changes that have taken place in Uttar Pradesh thereafter were portrayed.On the wall, artists used their colours and imagination to portray in paintings the changed positive environment in the state in terms of law and order, infrastructure and opportunities for youth. Young painter Manish Saroj’s painting expressed the pain of Uttar Pradesh suffering under mafia rule before 2017, while also presenting a positive picture of the change taking place now.Under the campaign, a comic distribution and dialogue programme will be organised in Muzaffarnagar tomorrow. During this, an original comic based on communal harmony will be distributed. Along with this, dialogues will also be held with youth in schools. On August 14, the song ‘Azadi from Fear’ of the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign will be launched. It will also feature a confluence of rap, music and digital art.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. President Droupadi Murmu has expressed grief over the loss of lives in the accident that occurred in Kaushambi district of Uttar Pradesh. In a social media post, she conveyed condolences to the families of those who lost their lives in this unfortunate incident. President Murmu also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also expressed grief over the loss of lives in the mishap. The Prime Minister also announced an ex-gratia of two lakh rupees from Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each deceased. The injured would be given 50 thousand rupees.

. Chemicals and Fertilizers Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda will inaugurate the two-week-long Swachhata Pakhwada-2026 today to raise awareness regarding the elimination of single-use plastics and promote the use of cloth bags and reusable bottles. The Pakhwada will be observed till the 15th of next month. The Department of Fertilizers said that the nationwide campaign aims to foster cleanliness at both physical and digital workplaces, promote environmental conservation, and bring qualitative improvements to work culture.It added that this year, alongside physical cleanliness, special priority is being accorded to Digital Cleanliness and Record Management to enhance administrative efficiency and transparency and further strengthen the e-filing system. Under this initiative, the e-Office and digital filing systems of the department will be streamlined, including reviewing pending e-files in the e-Office system, digitally closing or archiving disposed cases, and systematising databases.

. Defending champions Germany will take on Spain in the Men’s FIH Hockey World Cup 2026 final at the Belfius Hockey Arena in Wavre, Belgium, this evening. It is scheduled to start at 8 PM Indian Standard Time. While Germany will aim to defend the crown they won in 2023 and lift their fourth title, Spain will chase their maiden Hockey World Cup trophy.In the Women’s FIH World Cup final yesterday, Argentina defeated the Netherlands 3-1 in a penalty shoot-out after both teams were locked 1-1 in Amstelveen. Argentina snapped co-host the Netherlands’ dream run of a fourth consecutive and 10th overall World Cup title by winning the crown. Argentina, thus, avenged their last World Cup and Tokyo Olympics final defeat to win their third title.

. Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a 20-year Argentina career that included a World Cup triumph, two Copa América titles and a record 207 appearances for his country. Messi said the decision had been on his mind since the World Cup final defeat to Spain, before the death of his father further convinced him it was time to step away. The 39-year-old revealed the decision in a statement posted on his official Instagram account, confirming that he would no longer wear the Argentina jersey after one of the most celebrated international careers in football history.Messi said the decision had been painful, particularly because of the emotional bond he has shared with the national team and Argentina’s supporters throughout his career. He led his country to the World Cup title in 2022 after years of near misses and also helped Argentina win two Copa América crowns. His international journey also included World Cup final defeats in 2014 and again this summer, with the loss to Spain in July proving to be a significant moment in his decision-making process.

. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has shared details regarding the identification and repatriation of mortal remains of victims of the recent flash floods in Nepal. The Embassy said that, as per the Government of Nepal, several steps are required for handing over the mortal remains of foreign nationals.These include documentation of the mortal remains, recording photographs and details, post-mortem examination, verification of the cause of death, formal identification, collection of fingerprints, DNA and other forensic samples, verification of the deceased person’s passport or identity document, and completion of Embassy or consular coordination.The Embassy said that if relatives and family members are able to identify the mortal remains through photographs and descriptions available on the Nepal Police website, it will assist in coordinating with local authorities for the handover and repatriation of the mortal remains. It added that the Government of Nepal has carried out temporary interment of a large number of mortal remains to prevent health risks. The identification of such remains would require DNA matching with first-degree relatives.In cases where identification is not possible or the mortal remains have been temporarily interred, the Government will facilitate DNA matching. The Embassy said that people requiring assistance can contact the Embassy on the helpline at +977 985 131 6807, +977 970 910 7500, and +977 981 032 6117.

. In Nagaland, the 10th Edition of the Capt (Late) N Kenguruse, Mahavir Chakra Memorial Football Tournament 2026-27 will be held from November 2 to 10. The tournament will be conducted under the aegis of Spear Corps and Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (North), in collaboration with the Nagaland Football Association and supported by the Kohima District Football Association and Chümoukedima District Football Association.A total of 20 teams are expected to participate, divided into four pools of five teams each.  Matches will be played at Indira Gandhi Stadium, Kohima, and Chümoukedima Football Stadium. The tournament carries a total prize pool of 8.69 lakh rupees. Registrations will open today and close at 08:00 PM on 30 September. The tournament will culminate with the closing ceremony on November 10. The milestone edition seeks to celebrate football, inspire young talent and carry forward the values of courage, dedication and sportsmanship associated with the late Captain N. Kenguruse.

. The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) has achieved a major milestone in its nationwide mission-mode drive for Mandatory Biometric Updates, completing more than two crore biometric updates for school children across the country. The special drive, initiated in September last year, has now covered over one lakh 56 thousand schools, enabling school children to complete their Aadhaar biometric. Electronics and IT Ministry said that this has helped Mandatory Biometric Updates service to reach children directly at their schools, making the process more accessible and convenient for crores of students.Aadhaar enrolment for children below five years captures demographic information and a photograph, while fingerprints and iris biometrics are not captured at that age as these biometrics are still developing. Mandatory Biometric Updates helps ensure that the child’s Aadhaar continues to have updated biometric information. The Biometric updates are required when a child attains the age of 5 years and again at 15 years. To encourage timely completion and make the service more accessible, UIDAI had waived the charges for  children in the 7 to 15 years age group from 1st October 2025, for a period of one year. The Ministry said that lack of Biometric Updates in Aadhaar may lead to difficulties while carrying out authentication for receiving benefits under various Government schemes, registering in competitive and university examinations.

The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of Ministry of Home Affairs has advised people against a rise in financial frauds through malicious Android applications masquerading as pornography apps. The Ministry said that these applications are being circulated mainly through advertisements on Facebook and Instagram under names such as Night Play, Reloop, Kyss, Vimo, Rivo, Nexo and Vixa, among other similar variants.The Ministry said that the malicious advertisements redirect users to websites containing pornographic content, where they are prompted to download APK files from sources outside the Google Play Store. It added that once installed, the applications seek sensitive permissions, including Accessibility access, which can enable attackers to take control of the device and potentially carry out financial fraud.The Ministry further said that some of these applications may also download additional packages by posing as an app update and may install a Virtual Private Network (VPN) that can route the user’s internet traffic through attacker-controlled servers. The malicious application may also prevent users from uninstalling it through device settings. The Ministry, in an advisory, has advised people to install applications only from the Google Play Store or other trusted app stores. Users have also been advised not to download APK files through advertisements, websites or suspicious links and not to grant Accessibility permission to unknown applications. It asked citizens to verify the device and confirm that the suspicious application has been removed. It added that if the app cannot be removed or returns after restarting, back up your important data and perform a Factory Reset.

. Rescue teams in Nepal are racing against time to reach more than 600 workers believed to be trapped in mud-filled tunnels at the Trishuli-3A hydropower site. Crews are using explosives, heavy machinery and air pumps to clear the tunnels and search for survivors. According to Nepal’s disaster management authority, 939 people have died, and 3,925 are missing, including 592 foreign nationals. So far, 279 people have been rescued from hydropower sites, while more than 11,000 people have been rescued across the country.The rescue operation is being supported by Nepalese and Chinese military teams, along with experts from India, South Korea and Australia. Severe flooding and landslides have made it difficult for rescuers to locate the buried tunnels. India has sent specialised teams to help with both rescue operations and the identification of victims. A 19-member Indian forensic team began work in Kathmandu, assisting with DNA testing to identify recovered remains.An Indian tunnel-rescue team is also working at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang. Experts are helping Nepalese authorities search for 933 workers and employees who have been missing since August 26, with many believed to be trapped inside the tunnels. At least 11 hydropower projects were damaged by the floods. Families say rescue efforts have been too slow and are urging authorities to act quickly. Downstream in Chitwan, nearly 300 bodies have been recovered from rivers. Many remain unidentified, so authorities are using DNA testing.Due to a shortage of freezers, some bodies have been temporarily buried until they can be identified. Nepal has asked several countries for help, including freezers, DNA-testing equipment, drones, bridges and specialised tunnel-rescue tools. A team of 18 Indian forensic experts is assisting with DNA identification. In Tibet, Chinese state media reports 16 deaths and 546 missing people.China has rejected claims that its hydropower projects caused the disaster, calling such allegations malicious speculation. The floods, believed to have been triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border, have caused widespread destruction, damaging homes, roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure across Nepal.

. The US has described India as a dynamic, strong and resilient economy after official data showed that India’s GDP grew by 7.8 per cent. In an interview with a news agency, White House Senior Deputy Press Secretary Kush Desai said the growth figures confirmed the Trump administration’s view of India as a fast-growing economic power. He said India’s large and expanding economy offers major opportunities for US companies and investors.The US administration also wants to encourage American investment in India and greater Indian investment in the United States. Desai said President Donald Trump considers ties with India highly important and has often spoken about his friendship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. On the proposed India-US trade agreement, Desai said negotiations have moved to technical-level discussions. The two sides are working to resolve details, including product classifications and tariff rules. Desai said the US remains optimistic about the agreement and wants to strengthen both the economic and political partnership with India.

. The Jal Shakti Ministry will host the two-day Department Summit in New Delhi today to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration. The Summit is the first in a series of Departmental Summits envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi as an innovative platform.The two-day Summit will focus on four key thematic pillars, including timely implementation of water infrastructure projects, Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari-Catch the Rain, source sustainability of drinking water systems and operation and maintenance of rural drinking water supply schemes under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The Ministry said that discussions will cover project implementation, inter-agency coordination, water conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, digital monitoring, asset management and strengthening community-led water governance.

. India is taking part in the two-day G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) meeting in Asheville, US, on its final day today. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is leading India’s delegation. The meeting, under the US G20 presidency, is focusing on global economic growth, financial stability, rising debt, trade, investment and reforms to the international financial system. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has stressed the need for stronger growth, higher investment and better productivity to tackle growing global debt.India is using the meeting to highlight the needs of emerging economies and promote sustainable growth, trade and investment. New Delhi also wants to strengthen economic ties with G20 countries and present India as a major hub for manufacturing, technology and innovation. The Indian finance ministers held talks with UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey on trade and investment cooperation on the sidelines of the Meet. She also met 3M CEO William Brown to discuss India’s manufacturing, technology and skilled workforce.The meeting also seen disagreements over Russia’s participation on its opening day yesterday. Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attended in person, while some European officials skipped the traditional group photograph. Siluanov also met US Treasury Secretary Bessent. China’s large trade surplus is another key issue, with the US pushing for more balanced global trade and greater domestic consumption in China.The US chose Asheville partly to highlight the recovery of western North Carolina after Hurricane Helene. The Main G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled to be held in Miami on December 14-15 this year. India’s participation reflects its growing influence in global economic discussions and its efforts to shape policies on trade, investment, growth and financial stability.

. New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi held a comprehensive review meeting with senior officials of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. In a social media post, Mr Joshi said that the meeting focused on accelerating India’s green growth and strengthening Renewable Energy initiatives across the country, with a special focus on the Northeastern States.The Minister also reviewed the implementation of key Central Government schemes, including PM Surya Ghar, PM KUSUM and PM-JANMAN, and discussed measures to address implementation challenges and unlock India’s renewable energy potential. On the occasion, Mr Joshi directed officials to further strengthen renewable energy activities, expand access to clean energy and ensure that the benefits of sustainable development reach every corner of the country in the journey towards a Viksit Bharat.

. The 4th Indo-German Environmental Forum will be held in New Delhi today to strengthen bilateral cooperation and facilitate multi-stakeholder exchange on environment and climate change. Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav, along with German Minister for Environment, Climate Protection, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety Carsten Schneider, will co-chair the forum.Both sides will discuss key issues relating to environmental protection and climate policy to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, exchange experiences and advance practical collaboration. The Forum will provide a platform for bilateral exchanges among policymakers, private-sector representatives, think tanks and other key stakeholders on environmental and climate cooperation between the two countries.

In Nepal, the death toll from last week’s devastating floods and mudslides has risen to 903, while more than 4,247 people remain untraceable.According to the Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, the figure has increased from Sunday’s figure of 2,502. Bodies have been recovered from all eight affected districts of Nepal as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded.Meanwhile, at least 933 workers are believed to be trapped at around half a dozen hydropower projects. Rescue teams backed by India and other experts are searching around half a dozen blocked hydropower tunnels, including Trishuli-3A.  In Tibet, the death toll currently stands at 16, with 546 reported to be missing. The disaster sent a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris through towns and villages along the Nepal-Tibet border.An Indian tunnel rescue team is working with the Nepali Army at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang. Earth-moving machinery and soldiers have been working through the night to clear debris. Nepali Army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said the massive deposits are making tunnel access difficult.A preliminary study by Nepali scientists found the floods were triggered by a massive ice-rock avalanche at around 5,200 metres in Rasuwa’s Langtang-Lirung area. The debris entered the Lhende River before surging through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli.Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah called the floods an “unprecedented and devastating natural disaster”, with nearly 21,000 security personnel involved in rescue operations. The Red Cross estimates more than 90,000 people were affected, while authorities continue recovering and identifying bodies.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, along with other SCO leaders, participated in the official opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, last evening. The biennial event celebrates the rich sporting traditions, culture and heritage of nomadic civilisations, bringing together countries in a vibrant celebration of their shared culture.Earlier, Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings with leaders of Russia, Iran, the Kyrgyz Republic and Armenia on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit. The Prime Minister will address the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit today.

. Amid the floods in Nepal and the rising water levels of rivers in Bihar, the Animal and Fisheries Resources Department has advised people not to consume fish caught from floodwaters. According to the department, during floods, fish may come into contact with sewage, dead animals and other contaminated substances, increasing the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and other pathogens. Consumption of such fish may be harmful to health.The department has clarified that fish caught from floodwaters should not be used for consumption until the floodwater has stabilised and the condition of water bodies has returned to normal. The department has also appealed to people not to consume fish that appear unknown or unusual. People have been advised to avoid buying, selling or consuming fish caught from floodwaters.

. Prime Minister of Belgium Bart De Wever will be on a three-day visit to India from tomorrow. During the visit, he will hold bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and regional and global issues of mutual interest. Prime Minister De Wever will also deliver a keynote address at a business event in the context of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA).He will also travel to Mumbai, where he will engage with various stakeholders, including those from the diamond, ports and logistics sectors. The External Affairs Ministry said the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the India-Belgium partnership. It will also advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence and security, technology, renewable energy, connectivity and people-to-people ties. The ministry added that it will further deepen India-EU and India-Europe engagement.

All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

The International Cricket Council (ICC) has taken away the hosting rights of the inaugural edition of the Women’s Champions Trophy to be held in 2027 from Sri Lanka due to government interference in the administration of Sri Lanka Cricket. According to a report, Sri Lanka was set to host the first-ever edition of the women’s tournament, featuring six teams, including the hosts. But the decision could impact their participation as well. The report added that the ICC is likely to decide on the venue of the tournament in its next board meeting, with the move to strip Sri Lanka from hosting the competition set to make a financial impact on the board. The change of venue is also likely to see the Sri Lanka Women’s team possibly missing out on participating, as the tournament was set to host top five teams along with the host nation.

. India and Bangladesh today discussed issues of mutual interest with the aim of advancing people-to-people cooperation. The discussions took place during a meeting between India’s High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, and Adviser to Bangladesh’s Prime Minister for the Ministry of Finance and Planning, Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, in Dhaka. In a social media post, India’s High Commission in Bangladesh gave this information. Earlier on 25th August, Mr. Trivedi met Bangladesh’s Minister of Commerce, Industries, Textiles and Jute Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, where the two sides discussed various aspects of bilateral economic and commercial cooperation and explored ways to deepen ties between the two countries.

. In the FIH Men’s Hockey World Cup 2026, Germany retained the World Cup title with a 1-0 win over Spain in the final at the Belfius Hockey Arena in Wavre, Belgium, this evening. Michel Struthoff scored the only goal of the tightly contested final late in the third quarter, converting Germany’s only opportunity of a match largely controlled by Spain. His goal secured Germany’s fourth men’s World Cup title.Spain, appearing in their first World Cup final since 1998, enjoyed the greater share of possession and created more chances for long stretches but were unable to find a way through the German defence.Earlier today, Argentina defeated the Netherlands 2-1 to claim the men’s bronze medal.

. The Baloch National Movement (BNM) staged a protest in the Netherlands’ Utrecht city, drawing international attention to the ongoing abuses by Pakistani forces in Balochistan, including the enforced disappearance of thousands of people, extrajudicial killings and other serious human rights violations. The demonstration held yesterday to mark the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances brought together several political activists, who expressed solidarity with the victims of enforced disappearances and their families.The International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances is observed every year on August 30, a UN-designated day established in 2011 to raise global awareness of this grave human rights violation and to honour the victims and their families. According to the BNM, the protesters held photographs of forcibly disappeared persons and carried banners and placards while demanding justice and calling for an immediate end to enforced disappearances in Balochistan. Addressing the gathering, the speakers highlighted the profound and devastating impact of enforced disappearances on Baloch society, saying hardly any family in Balochistan has remained untouched by the trauma of enforced disappearance.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the 26th annual Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in the capital city of Kyrgyzstan, Bishkek. The discussions focused on key areas of India-Russia bilateral cooperation, including trade and investment, energy and defence.During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi said it was a matter of deep satisfaction that cooperation between India and Russia continued to scale new heights.On the Ukraine conflict, PM Modi stressed the need for a peaceful resolution, saying that every day of war sets humanity back. He told President Putin that resolving all issues through peaceful means is a call of humanity. PM Modi said, ” We must move from endless wars to ending wars,’ adding that India supports all efforts towards peace.The meeting took place more than a week before President Putin is scheduled to travel to India to attend the annual BRICS summit.During the meeting, the Prime Minister said India is hosting the BRICS Summit in a few days, and all Indians are eager to welcome Mr Putin and his delegation. He said the visit of the Russian President will strengthen bilateral relations and further reinforce dialogue and cooperation within the BRICS framework.President Vladimir Putin showed his satisfaction that Indian-Russian relations continue to strengthen on the basis of the principles of a special and privileged partnership.
